title: A block case that yields its value

blocks.text: When an arm of a switch expression needs several statements, it becomes a block, and the block gives the arm's value with `yield`:
Write `code(String status, List<String> alerts)` in `Status` as one switch expression. The status is matched in any case:

items: `"error"` adds one alert, `"alert: "` followed by the status as given, to `alerts`, and gives `-1`;
any other status gives `0` and raises no alert.

blocks.text: Examples: `code("SUCCESS", alerts)` is `1`; `code("Error", alerts)` is `-1` and leaves `alerts` holding `"alert: Error"`; `code("pending", alerts)` is `0`.

cases.says: success, error and pending give 1, -1 and 0.
An error adds exactly one alert, and nothing else adds any.

concepts: A case that needs several statements uses a block and gives its value with yield.
